00014| 
00015| The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
00016| 
00017| ## Usage
00018| 
00019| To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
00020| 
00021| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
00022| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00023| 
00024| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00025|   cacheComponents: true,
00026| }
00027| 
00028| export default nextConfig
00029| ```
00030| 
00031| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
00032| const nextConfig = {
00033|   cacheComponents: true,
00034| }
00035| 
00036| export default nextConfig
00037| ```
00038| 
00039| The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
00040| 
00041| ```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
00042| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00043| 
00044| export async function getData() {
00045|   'use cache'
00046|   cacheTag('my-data')
00047|   const data = await fetch('/api/data')
00048|   return data
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
00053| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00054| 
00055| export async function getData() {
00056|   'use cache'
00057|   cacheTag('my-data')
00058|   const data = await fetch('/api/data')
00059|   return data
00060| }
00061| ```
00062| 
00063| You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
00064| 
00065| - Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
00066| - Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
00067| 
00068| For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
00069| 
00070| ```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
00071| 'use server'
00072| 
00073| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00074| 
00075| export default async function submit() {
00076|   await addPost()
00077|   updateTag('my-data')
00078| }
00079| ```

00083|

00085|

00087|   await addPost()

00089| }
00090| ```

00094| - **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.

00098| cacheTag('tag-one', 'tag-two')

00114| }

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

Implemented the admin catalog page with background sync.

- `next.config.ts` — enabled `cacheComponents: true`
- `lib/products.ts` — cached catalog fetch with `'use cache'` and `cacheTag('products')`
